name: ArtifactsBench
description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifacts. It contains 1,825 executable queries across nine primary topics and uses an automated multimodal evaluation pipeline with checklist-guided MLLM-as-Judge scoring based on code, visuals, and interaction.
creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
citeAs: ArtifactsBench: Bridging the Visual-Interactive Gap in LLM Code Generation Evaluation
rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was curated through a multi-stage pipeline combining expert sourcing with LLM generation and refinement. Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters removed incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Tasks were validated for solvability and ambiguity, and revised or removed if underspecified or solvable only by brittle hacks.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Candidate tasks were sourced from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication and contamination control were applied: (i) MinHash plus semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Difficulty was assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs to enforce a 30%/40%/30% Easy/Medium/Hard split. Sub-categories were tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrote prompts for clarity, completeness, and executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks were revised or removed. Execution was standardized with headless Chromium (Playwright) at 1024 x 768 resolution and deterministic seeds, and three staged screenshots were captured before, during, and after scripted interaction.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query was paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists were LLM-drafted and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchored calibration and was reused as few-shot references. In human validation, 280 queries with outputs from 6 models were independently scored by multiple front-end engineers in a double-blind protocol, and the final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Checklist calibration achieved Cohen's kappa >= 0.8 among annotators on a 10% manually curated seed. Human validation used Pair ACC to measure agreement between automated referees and human judges over pairwise model response rankings. The final human ground-truth score was the median of individual annotators' ratings. The paper also reports cross-judge robustness between Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B and version stability for Gemini.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience; front-end engineers; human annotators
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. The paper states they release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings. It discusses replacing the deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with the stable Gemini-2.5-Pro and reports identical ordering constraints, but no explicit update schedule or deprecation policy for the dataset itself is provided.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The query quality filtering prompt explicitly aims to select privacy-free queries and avoid sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models and to better evaluate visual fidelity and interactive integrity that affect real-world user experience and adoption.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that multimodal LLM judges can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, version drift, and potential cognitive biases in interpreting long-horizon interaction logic and dynamic visual feedback. It also notes that referee evaluation criteria may diverge from human judgments.
rai:dataLimitations: The current methodology evaluates dynamic behavior using a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions such as multi-step workflows or nuanced game physics. The benchmark focuses on the final artifact generated in a single turn and does not assess iterative agentic refinement, self-debugging, or multi-step development processes.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual artifact generation. It is used to evaluate over 30 models at scale, analyze performance across interactivity levels and task categories, validate automated referees against human experts, and provide fine-grained diagnostics on strengths and failure modes.
